evidence: app/package.json:13 — nitro pinned to ^3.0.261029-rc (RC), the production server for npm start
app/package.json:10-11 — @solidjs/start 2.1.0 / vite ^8.0.0: framework stable only since 2026-08-04, used in every route
app/vite.config.ts:4-6 — no experimental flags; ssr:false and devOverlay:false are documented stable options
reach.rationale: No experimental/unstable names or flags in app code, but the app's whole runtime rests on a framework that became stable ~3 months ago plus one RC server dependency; that fits 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:5 — nitro() invoked with zero Nitro-specific options, the only RC touchpoint besides the pin
app/src/routes/api-proxy/[...path].ts:3 — server routes written against @solidjs/start/server APIEvent, not Nitro/h3 APIs
app/src/routes/media/[...path].ts:3 — same: plain Web-standard fetch/Response behind SolidStart's handler contract
containment.rationale: The RC dependency is confined to package.json and one vite.config.ts line with no Nitro API surface; swapping or upgrading it would not touch any of the 19 source files.

evidence: app/package.json:13 + app/vite.config.ts:5 — Nitro v3 is the officially documented deployment plugin for SolidStart v2 (docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/guides/deployment-plugins); no stable alternative exists
app/src/routes/index.tsx:22 — long-stable createResource instead of newer createAsync/query APIs, the conservative choice
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:41-49 — plain createResource + createMemo for query-string state; no experimental primitives anywhere
justification.rationale: The only non-stable dependency is mandated by the framework's current docs and buys production serving that nothing stable provides; everything else is long-stable Solid APIs, so no use is gratuitous.

findings.issue: Production server (npm start) runs on nitro 3.0.261029-rc, a pre-1.0-style RC channel (npm dist-tag 'latest' is itself an RC; v3 is still not the declared stable line)
findings.suggestion: Keep nitro pinned in package-lock and schedule a bump when nitro 3.0 final lands; subscribe to nitro v3 release notes since breaking changes can still occur on the RC channel.

findings.issue: The entire app sits on SolidStart v2 / Vite 8, stable only since Aug 2026 / Mar 2026 respectively, so ecosystem churn risk is elevated versus an older line
findings.suggestion: Pin exact versions in the lockfile and plan for patch/minor upgrades within the first year; the app's small, non-exotic API surface makes this cheap.

findings.issue: ssr: false is a stable documented option, but it relies on SolidStart v2's newly rewritten SPA entrypoints, which have known early bugs (e.g. open PR #2312 around dev-overlay navigation)
findings.suggestion: Stay on current @solidjs/start patch releases; if dev-mode hydration issues appear, devOverlay: false (already set) is the right workaround.

summary: The app is conservative: zero experimental markers, directives or config flags, and it uses only long-stable Solid primitives instead of the framework's newer data APIs. Its single non-stable dependency is the Nitro v3 RC, which is exactly the deployment plugin SolidStart v2's official docs mandate, fully confined to package.json and vite.config.ts. The residual risk is that SolidStart v2 (stable Aug 2026) and Nitro v3 (still RC) are both very new, so lockfile discipline matters.
